clue.text: A 28 visit Greek 20 to "grow together"

parts.note: entry 28 is a hundred, and C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
entry 20 means a piece of land in the sea, and Crete is a Greek one

explanation.surface: A hundred tourists visit a Greek isle to bond with one another.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-references do the work: 28 is HUNDRED, giving C, and 20 is ISLAND, so a Greek one is CRETE. 'visit' merely links.
explanation.definitionFit: To accrete is to grow by accumulation, particles adhering and fusing into a single mass.

clue.text: Grand Emperor's ignoring us

indicators.note: ignoring something means leaving it out, so the word us is dropped from the emperor's name

parts.note: Augustus was the first Roman emperor

explanation.surface: A grand emperor pays no attention to the rest of us.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the final US from AUGUSTUS leaves the adjective; 'Grand' looks like a title for the emperor but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, august means majestic, dignified and imposing, a synonym for grand.

clue.text: Where Father Ted was caught with raging gays, darling

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: raging suggests wild disorder, so the letters of gays and darling are thrown about

explanation.surface: A priest is caught out among a crowd of flamboyant gay men, calling them darling.
explanation.walkthrough: Father Ted is a 1990s sitcom about three priests exiled to a fictional parish off the west coast of Ireland. 'raging' looks like an adjective for the crowd but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The sitcom's priests lived on this fictional windswept outpost, the setting of the whole series.

clue.text: Seasonal fare in 8, cooked by galley slave originally

indicators.note: cooked means prepared or altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: entry 8 is the cheapest passenger accommodation on a ship

indicators.note: originally means taking the first letters of galley and slave

explanation.surface: Holiday food is prepared below decks by a ship's galley slave.
explanation.walkthrough: Answer 8 is STEERAGE; 'cooked' rearranges it into EASTEREG, then 'originally' adds G and S, the starts of 'galley slave'. 'in' and 'by' merely link.
explanation.definitionFit: Chocolate confections given at Easter are the typical festive treat of that spring season.

clue.text: Old Irishman, one living abroad

parts.note: ex means former, as in an ex-wife
Pat, short for Patrick, is a stock name for an Irishman

explanation.surface: An elderly Irishman who has emigrated.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for expatriate, someone who lives outside their native country.

clue.text: Catholics disparagingly said to be sanctimonious in earlier times

indicators.note: in places the word for sanctimonious inside the word for earlier times

parts.note: pasts are bygone periods or earlier times
pi is informal shorthand for pious, meaning sanctimonious or self-righteous

explanation.surface: Catholics were in former days scornfully described as self-righteous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said to be' is a link joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A derogatory term for Roman Catholics, alluding to their allegiance to the Pope.

clue.text: New Cypriot zoo lacks one unknown type of primitive animal

indicators.note: new signals that the letters of Cypriot zoo are made into something fresh

parts.note: in algebra x, y and z are unknowns, and y is one of them

explanation.surface: A recently opened zoo in Cyprus is missing one mysterious species of early creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges the letters, and 'lacks' removes the unknown, which in algebra is conventionally x, y or z; only Y fits the leftover letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Protozoic describes the protozoa, single-celled organisms regarded as the most primitive animal forms.

clue.text: Annual event for the Irish setter (nothing at all Irish)

parts.note: Puck is the pseudonym of this puzzle's setter
FA, as in sweet FA, is a coy euphemism for nothing at all

explanation.surface: The setter, himself Irish, pretends a yearly festival means nothing to him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Irish setter' looks like the dog breed, but it is the setter of this puzzle. PUCK FAIR is a festival held every August in Killorglin, County Kerry, where a goat is crowned king.
explanation.definitionFit: This three-day gathering in County Kerry is held every August and is one of Ireland's oldest festivals.

clue.text: Indian hunters trek endlessly in their women's clothes

indicators.note: in puts the shortened trek inside the clothes

parts.note: saris are the draped garments worn by Indian women

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the word for trek is dropped

parts.note: a hike is a long walk or trek

explanation.surface: Indian hunters make a long journey dressed in their wives' saris.
explanation.definitionFit: In India a shikari is a hunter, especially one who guides big-game hunting expeditions.

clue.text: Emasculated creature facing eternity where the poor Titanic passengers nightly lay

definitions.text: where the poor Titanic passengers nightly lay

parts.note: a steer is a castrated bull
an age is an extremely long time, loosely an eternity

explanation.surface: A bullock faces eternity in the cheap berths of the doomed liner.
explanation.definitionFit: Steerage was the cheapest, lowest deck accommodation on liners, where poorer emigrants slept.

clue.text: Billy's relatives attempt a way back

parts.note: a go is an attempt, as in have a go

indicators.note: back signals that the abbreviation for way is turned round

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Someone tries to retrace the route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Billy' is a billy goat, so his relatives are others of his kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A billy is a male of the species, so the herd of nannies and kids are his kin.

clue.text: Ban writing in bed? On the contrary

indicators.note: in proposes putting the writing inside the bed
on the contrary reverses that proposal, so the bed goes inside the writing instead

parts.note: prose is ordinary written language
a crib is a child's bed

explanation.surface: A ban on writing while lying in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the clue puts the writing inside the bed; 'On the contrary' flips that so the bed goes inside the writing.
explanation.definitionFit: To proscribe is to forbid or outlaw, so it works as a verb meaning ban.

clue.text: Drug-fuelled Madness member into mad idea

indicators.note: fuelled means the singer is filled with the drug letter

parts.note: Suggs is the lead singer of the British ska band Madness
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

indicators.note: mad signals that the letters of into are scrambled

explanation.surface: A drugged-up band member gets into some crazy notion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Madness' is a 1980s British ska band whose singer is SUGGS; 'mad' rearranges INTO to make TION.
explanation.definitionFit: A suggestion is a proposal or notion put forward for consideration.

clue.text: See 6
Place in West of Kerry one left rolling drunk?

indicators.note: in a down entry the west of a word is read as its start, so the first letter of Kerry

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: drunk signals that the letters are tipsily rearranged

explanation.surface: A town in western County Kerry where someone has been left reeling, very drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Kerry is a county in the southwest of Ireland. 'drunk' rearranges I, L and ROLLING after K.
explanation.definitionFit: This small town on the River Laune in County Kerry is the home of the annual goat fair.

clue.text: Personifying two setters, vocalise strangled cat on record

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: strangled means the cat is gripped between the two setters

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as I, here twice
the second of the two setters, another I
a tom is a male cat
to sing is to vocalise

explanation.surface: A setter impersonating himself and a colleague yowls like a cat being throttled on a recording.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter calls himself I, so two setters are two I's; 'strangled' has them grip the cat between them, and 'on record' puts the record first.
explanation.definitionFit: To epitomise is to be the perfect example of, so it means embodying or personifying.

clue.text: Some final changes for a 20

definitions.note: entry 20 refers to a piece of land surrounded by sea

indicators.note: changes signals that the letters of some final are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some last-minute alterations for a certain spot.
explanation.definitionFit: This Crown dependency lies in the Irish Sea between Britain and Ireland, a single body of land ringed by water.

clue.text: Audacity shown by Bill wearing the French woman's jewellery

parts.note: neck is British slang for cheek or audacity

indicators.note: wearing means the French word has the bill inside it, like clothes worn

parts.note: le is French for the
AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: A man brazenly wears a Frenchwoman's jewels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the French woman's' reads as one phrase, but 'the French' gives LE and 'woman's jewellery' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A necklace is an ornament worn around the neck, a typical piece of a woman's jewels.

clue.text: Wood panelling of cask cut in two, accidentally

indicators.note: accidentally signals the letters fall into a haphazard order
cut means the end of cask is chopped off

explanation.surface: Wooden panels made from a barrel accidentally sawn in half.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks the K of CASK; 'accidentally' rearranges CAS with IN and TWO.
explanation.definitionFit: Wainscot is wooden lining on the lower part of an interior wall.

clue.text: Heaving cleavage in front of large, born-again Christian?

indicators.note: heaving means tossing about, so the letters are rearranged
front of means only the first letter of large is taken

explanation.surface: A heaving bosom up front does not suit a born-again believer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heaving' rearranges CLEAVAGE with IN and L, the front of 'large'.
explanation.definitionFit: Evangelical Christians stress personal conversion, the experience of being reborn in faith.

clue.text: Wrong route, right car

indicators.note: wrong signals that the letters of route are put in the incorrect order

explanation.surface: The road's wrong, but the vehicle's right.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourer is a car designed for long-distance touring, such as an open-topped model.

clue.text: See 2
Related to 9's leader, this 6 is 13's top one

parts.note: kin means related, as in kin to someone

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of answer 9

explanation.surface: Related to the head billy, this festival figure is the town's chief.
explanation.walkthrough: At PUCK FAIR (6) in KILLORGLIN (13) a wild goat is crowned King Puck and presides over the festival.
explanation.definitionFit: The goat crowned at the fair is called King Puck, the ruling monarch of the town for three days.

clue.text: Bill has one horse? Not the case for bums

parts.note: a bill is a printed notice or poster
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer letters, so without them only the middle of horse remains

explanation.surface: Bill owns a horse, but that isn't the reason for the layabouts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not the case' strips the outer letters of HORSE, leaving ORS.
explanation.definitionFit: Posteriors is a jocular word for the buttocks, which is what bums means in British slang.

clue.text: Fraction of wine used by hotel

parts.note: tent is a deep red Spanish wine
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Part of the wine is used by a hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: One part in ten is a specific fraction, a decile portion of a whole.

clue.text: Odd bits of invective needed — for this CD, that is

definitions.text: Odd bits of invective needed — for this CD, that is

parts.words: Odd bits of invective needed — for this CD, that is
parts.note: IV and C are odd bits of the word invective, and as Roman numerals IV followed by C means the number CD

explanation.surface: A music review needs a few odd scraps of abuse for this album.
explanation.walkthrough: CD looks like a compact disc, but it is the Roman numeral; IV and C, scattered bits of 'invective', are Roman four and hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: CD in Roman numerals is D (five hundred) less C (one hundred), the number written in words here.

clue.text: Runner, last of four to get TV role

definitions.meaning: the anchor runs the final leg of a four-person relay
a news presenter who links the programme's reports

explanation.surface: An athlete running the final relay leg lands a part on television.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses name the person in the key final position: last in a relay, or presenting the news.

clue.text: Grub of spectacular variety

indicators.note: of indicates the letters are taken out of the phrase spectacular variety

explanation.surface: A grub of extraordinary kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A grub is the soft wormlike young of an insect, the stage before metamorphosis.

clue.text: Some guts by cricket side to go in first

indicators.note: first places the word for going in ahead of the cricket side

parts.note: to enter is to go in
on is the leg side of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A cricketer next to the leg side goes in to bat first, needing nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guts' looks like courage, but here it means intestines. In cricket the ON side is the half of the field behind the batter's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: The enteron is the alimentary canal, the digestive tube running through an animal's body.
